=== DOCS-VERIFICATION (trino.io/docs/467 via WebFetch) ===
• first_value / last_value are WINDOW functions (verified at trino.io/docs/467/functions/window.html — Value functions section): they return one value PER INPUT ROW from inside the window FRAME; they do NOT collapse rows. They require an OVER clause; they cannot be used as plain aggregates under GROUP BY.
• min_by(x, y) / max_by(x, y) are AGGREGATE functions (verified at trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html — General aggregate functions): 'Returns the value of x associated with the maximum/minimum value of y over all input values.' They collapse to ONE ROW per GROUP BY group — exactly the shape the 'first AND last value of a column per entity in one row' question asks for.
• Trino GROUP BY analyzer rule (trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html): 'When a GROUP BY clause is used in a SELECT statement all output expressions must be either aggregate functions or columns present in the GROUP BY clause.' → a window function in the SELECT list that references a column not in GROUP BY and not wrapped in an aggregate is INVALID.
• Canonical one-row-per-group 'first AND last value of a column' form = min_by(col, ts) AS first_val, max_by(col, ts) AS last_val ... GROUP BY entity (aggregates). The window first_value/last_value form WITHOUT GROUP BY yields one row per input row → needs SELECT DISTINCT to collapse.
